previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, and tracheostomy dependence was admitted for increased respiratory secretions and suspected pneumonia after transfer from an outside ICU. He was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics, with sputum cultures confirming Pseudomonas and Klebsiella. Treatment was adjusted to IV Zosyn based on sensitivities, and oral vancomycin was added for C. diff prophylaxis. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic administration. His condition stabilized with improved respiratory status and no fever. HIV testing showed a viral load of 101 copies/mL and a CD4 count of 106. Orthopedic evaluation revealed worsening right hip osteoarthritis and foot inversion due to deconditioning, with recommendations for physical therapy. He was discharged to extended care to complete his antibiotic course and continue rehabilitation.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old male with a history of AIDS (last CD4 ___, VL 
101 copies/ml ___ complicated by multiple infections and 
resulting aphasia, chronic respiratory failure requiring trach 
and PEG, recurrent c. diff, with recent hospitalization ___ 
for klebsiella and pseudomonas pneumonia presenting from long 
term living facility with fever, tachypnea, hypotension, and 
leukocytosis found to have pseudomonal UTI on urine culture 
concerning for urosepsis.

ACTIVE ISSUES
=============

#Pseudomonal Urosepsis: 
Given positive sputum culture for pseudomonas, his sepsis was 
initially thought to be due to pseudomonas pneumonia. However, 
his urine culture from ___ showed WBC >182 with >100,000 
organisms/mL of pseudomonas. Thus he was treated for pseudomonal 
urosepsis. A superimposed pneumonia or opportunistic infection 
is possible though unlikely given chest ___ findings and AIDS 
ppx, and his respiratory status quickly returned to his baseline 
with suctioning. He was placed on IV Zosyn 4.5g q8h. His 
pseudomonal UTI was subsequently found to be sensitive to zosyn, 
cefepime, ceftazidime, leaving no oral options since resistant 
to ciprofloxacin. He will need IV antibiotics for 8 days. Stool 
studies for c diff, yersinia, vibrio, O&P as well as blood 
cultures pending at the time of discharge. 

#Tachypnea/increased secretions: 
His symptoms were suspected to be due to chronic interstitial 
lung injury. His respiratory status improved during the 
hospitalization with suctioning of secretions though he remained 
mildly tachypneic. Respiratory therapy confirmed that trach cuff 
is inflated and ___ position. We continued frequent tracheal tube 
suctioning and humidified air mask, along with albuterol 
nebulizer treatments q2h prn and ipratropium q6h.  

#History of C diff: 
ID recommended PO vancomycin during previous admission for C 
diff ppx. He was thus placed on 125mg vancomycin PO q6h. ID 
recommended continuing PO vancomycin 125mg q6h for 7 days after 
last dose of Zosyn.  After this he will return to his 
prophylactic dose of 250 mg PO BID.

caused your symptoms, and you improved markedly after receiving 
antibiotics.  The infectious disease team was consulted and 
recommended continuing your treatment with IV antibiotics for 
the urinary tract infection, so we placed a type of temporary IV 
___ your arm called a midline.  Given your history of C. diff 
diarrhea, we are treating you with an oral antibiotic that you 
will keep taking for another week after finishing IV 
antibiotics.  You have a follow up with orthopedics for your 
arthritis.
